dimensions.note: The model accepts no credentials and uses no vault. Strict schemas, public/internal sensitivity bounds, and recursive key/text denylist checks reject common credential, personal-data, URL, IP, and raw-payload leakage before persistence.
Three structured lifecycle logs contain only schema-validated resource-safe snapshot IDs and no source summaries or payloads.
Schema, leakage, consistency, freshness, malformed input, conflicting replay, and storage failures propagate without a success result; validation diagnostics are stable and sorted.

Twelve passing tests cover persistence, strict leakage denial, denylist patterns, sensitivity, freshness, replay, storage failure, attestation accounting, safe names, provenance ambiguity, cyclic input, and zero authority.
Identical replay performs no write and returns no handle; same-ID content changes fail closed. Storage failures are not swallowed or represented as success.
This provider-neutral validation boundary performs no external API calls; provider adapters remain outside the extension.
The extension opens no network connection, process, file, stream, or other external resource.
The archive exposes one model plus README and MIT license. Fixtures and examples are synthetic and contain no live provider, account, endpoint, credential, or customer data.

The persisted envelope and every nested object are strict. IDs, counts, rows, bytes, windows, timestamps, source identity, evidence uniqueness, traversal, redaction, filtering, and authority are bounded and cross-validated.
The sole immutable snapshot resource declares lifetime 30d and garbageCollection 10.
The contract intentionally supports immutable validated snapshot persistence rather than a mutable CRUD lifecycle.
Complete schema, leakage, allowlist-accounting, freshness, redaction, authority, provenance, and replay checks precede the sole write.
Resource names are deterministic snapshot-<snapshotId>; snapshotId now permits only resource-safe letters, numbers, colon, dot, underscore, and hyphen.
Replay detection uses context.readResource and persistence uses context.writeResource; implementation never accesses Swamp storage directly.
The extension is unpublished. Version 2026.08.24.1 is the registry-proposed first publication version, so no persisted published-version upgrade exists.
